key_insight: Confined active particles can reorganize and destabilize an elastic vesicle, producing a sequence of activity-driven shape transitions from ordered deformation to turbulent self-stirring.
engineering_relevance: The work shows how membrane mechanics and active-fluid forcing can be coupled to tune soft encapsulated systems, with implications for synthetic cells, microcapsules, and active soft-matter devices.
method: Modeled a 2D weakly extensible elastic vesicle with bending rigidity in a Stokes flow.
Described the enclosed dilute extensile active suspension with kinetic theory and weak anchoring at the membrane.
Validated the theory with nonlinear volume-conserving immersed boundary simulations across activity thresholds.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a closed-form quiescent equilibrium, a stability analysis predicting ordered instability thresholds, and simulations that reveal distinct regimes: spindle, rotor, fluctuating spinner, and turbulent self-stirring.
watch_item: Results are based on a 2D model with weak anchoring and idealized active particles, so quantitative behavior may shift in 3D or with stronger membrane–particle coupling.
paper_title: Active Sculpting: morphodynamics of internally stirred active vesicles
